# Micah 7 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA (Council Arbiter) | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Leningrad Codex (B19A)

---

**1** Woe is me! For I have become as when the summer fruit has been gathered, as when the grapes have been gleaned: there is no cluster to eat, no first-ripe fig that my soul desires.

**2** The godly has perished from the earth, and there is no one upright among mankind; they all lie in wait for blood, and each hunts the other with a net.

**3** Their hands are on what is evil, to do it well; the prince and the judge ask for a bribe, and the great man utters the evil desire of his soul; thus they weave it together.

**4** The best of them is like a brier, the most upright of them a thorn hedge. The day of your watchmen, of your punishment, has come; now their confusion shall come.

**5** Put no trust in a neighbor; have no confidence in a friend; guard the doors of your mouth from her who lies in your arms;

**6** For the son treats the father with contempt, the daughter rises up against her mother, the daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law; a man's enemies are the men of his own household.

**7** But as for me, I will look to the LORD; I will wait for the God of my salvation; my God will hear me.

**8** Rejoice not over me, O my enemy; when I fall, I shall rise; when I sit in darkness, the LORD will be a light to me.

**9** I will bear the indignation of the LORD because I have sinned against Him, until He pleads my cause and executes judgment for me. He will bring me out to the light; I shall look upon His vindication.

**10** Then my enemy will see, and shame will cover her who said to me, "Where is the LORD your God?" My eyes will look upon her; now she will be trampled down like the mire of the streets.

**11** A day for the building of your walls! In that day the boundary shall be far extended.

**12** In that day they will come to you, from Assyria and the cities of Egypt, and from Egypt to the River, from sea to sea and from mountain to mountain.

**13** But the earth will be desolate because of its inhabitants, for the fruit of their deeds.

**14** Shepherd Your people with Your staff, the flock of Your inheritance, who dwell alone in a forest in the midst of a garden land; let them graze in Bashan and Gilead as in the days of old.

**15** As in the days when you came out of the land of Egypt, I will show them marvelous things.

**16** The nations shall see and be ashamed of all their might; they shall lay their hands on their mouths; their ears shall be deaf.

**17** They shall lick the dust like a serpent, like the crawling things of the earth; they shall come trembling out of their strongholds; they shall turn in dread to the LORD our God, and they shall be in fear of You.

**18** Who is a God like You, pardoning iniquity and passing over transgression for the remnant of His inheritance? He does not retain His anger forever, because He delights in steadfast love.

**19** He will again have compassion on us; He will tread our iniquities underfoot. You will cast all our sins into the depths of the sea.

**20** You will show faithfulness to Jacob and steadfast love to Abraham, as You have sworn to our fathers from the days of old.

---
## SOPHIA's Council Notes

SOPHIA detected **6** significant divergence(s) in Micah 7.

- **7:1** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS renders formal English; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary audience.

- **7:5** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS renders formal English; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary audience.

- **7:7** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS renders formal English; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary audience.

- **7:8** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS renders formal English; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary audience.

- **7:13** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS renders formal English; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary audience.

- **7:19** — EMET preserves Hebrew word-order; LOGOS renders formal English; PNEUMA interprets for contemporary audience.

## Translation Notes (Select)

### EMET
- **7:6**: Oyvei ish anshei veito — 'a man's enemies are the men of his household.' Quoted by Jesus in Matthew 10:36. Societal breakdown reaches its nadir when the family itself disintegrates.
- **7:18**: Mi El kamokha — 'Who is a God like You?' A wordplay on Micah's own name (Mi-ka-yah = 'Who is like YHWH?'). The book ends with the prophet's name becoming the theology — the incomparability of God who forgives.
- **7:19**: Ve-tashlikh bi-metzulot yam kol-chatotam — 'You will cast into the depths of the sea all their sins.' The tashlich imagery — sins drowned beyond recovery. This verse gives its name to the Jewish Rosh Hashanah ceremony of symbolically casting sins into water.

### LOGOS
- **7:7-10**: The prophetic voice shifts from communal lament (vv.1-6) to individual confidence (vv.7-10). Despite total social collapse, the prophet personally trusts in YHWH. This is faith as defiant hope.
- **7:18-20**: The book's doxological conclusion answers its opening question. Chapter 1 asks 'What is the transgression of Jacob?' Chapter 7 answers with who forgives that transgression — a God unlike any other.
- **7:19**: The 'depths of the sea' echoes the Red Sea deliverance (Exodus 15). The same waters that swallowed Egypt's army will swallow Israel's sins. Exodus imagery reframed as forgiveness.

### PNEUMA
- **7:7-8**: 'Though I fall, I will rise. Though I sit in darkness, the LORD is my light.' This is biblical hope distilled — not denial of suffering but confidence through it. Two of the most resilient verses in the Bible.
- **7:18**: The last question of the book is the best one: 'Who is a God like You?' — a God who pardons, who doesn't stay angry, who delights in mercy. That's the final word. Not judgment — mercy.
- **7:19**: Sins thrown into the deepest part of the ocean. Gone. Unretrievable. God doesn't just forgive — He disposes of the evidence permanently. The Jewish tashlich ceremony at Rosh Hashanah is built on this very image.

— SOPHIA
